newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-BARCELONA MUST RELY ON THIRD-CHOICE GOALKEEPER.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BARCELONA MUST RELY ON THIRD-CHOICE GOALKEEPER.

text.p: Barcelona are compelled to use third-choice goalkeeper Julen Lopetegui for their European Cup Winners' Cup quarter-final home leg against AIK Stockholm on Thursday.
Portuguese international keeper Vitor Baia suffered a neck injury in training on Tuesday, while reserve Carlos Busquets is still recovering from a knock.
Coach Bobby Robson was left with no choice but to call up Lopetegui, compounding the former England manager's problems.
Barcelona were rocked at the weekend by their 4-0 Spanish league defeat at Tenerife, a result that left Robson's side nine points adrift of leaders and arch-rivals Real Madrid.

Apart from Baia, Robson will also be without midfielder Oscar Garcia and possibly Portguese defender Fernando Couto through injury. Winger Emmanuel Amunike is cup-tied because of previous appearance for his former side, Sporting Lisbon.
But Robson will be able to call upon the services of key striker Ronaldo, who last missed last week's Spanish Cup game against Atletico Madrid because of international duty for Brazil.
Ronaldo may enjoy himself against AIK, a team seen by Barcelona pundits as one of the softest options remaining in the competition.
The theoretical quality gap between the two sides may become more evident because of the Swedes' lengthy winter lay-off.
But AIK manager Stefan Soderberg said on Monday he was pleased with his team's performance in a Scandinavian club competition held in Cyprus last week.
AIK reached the final, which they lost, but beat Norway's Lillestrom in the semifinal.
The Swedish club's line-up against Barcelona is due to be decided after training later on Wednesday following fitness checks on sick and injured players.
A club spokeswoman said Krister Nordin, Ola Andersson and Thomas Lagerlof had colds and temperatures but were improving, while Nebojsa Novakovic was suffering from an Achilles tendon problem.
Three of the four are midfielders.
"We have not yet decided on the final team but it looks as if they will all be better by tomorrow," the spokeswoman said.
